questions.q: What does least privilege mean, generalized from Lesson 44's environment permissions?
options: Every person and automated process gets exactly the access needed to do its job, and no more — applied to individual grants, not just environment-wide defaults
Only administrators should ever have any access to production systems
Every environment should have identical permissions regardless of purpose
Access should be granted broadly to avoid slowing down incident response
questions.explain: Lesson 44 applied this to dev/test/prod defaults; this lesson generalizes it to individual access grants.

questions.q: Why does permission creep happen even when nobody involved does anything wrong?
options: Granting access is a deliberate action, while revoking it almost never is unless something forces the question
Permission creep only happens due to malicious insider activity
Fabric automatically grants excessive permissions by default
It only happens when engineers deliberately ignore security policy
questions.explain: Each individual grant was reasonable at the time it was made — the problem is accumulation over time with no automatic expiration.

questions.q: What is an access review, and what does it structurally resemble?
options: A recurring, scheduled check of who still needs their current access — the same structural pattern as Lesson 55's capacity right-sizing
A one-time setup step performed only when a workspace is first created
An automated tool that requires no human judgment at all
A process only relevant to secrets, not to broader access grants
questions.explain: Access needs, like compute needs, drift away from whatever was true when the grant was first made.

questions.q: Why does an access review treat "not sure" the same as "no" when deciding whether to revoke a grant?
options: The burden of justifying continued access should sit with keeping it, not with revoking it
"Not sure" responses are always false positives and should be ignored
Access reviews should always default to keeping every grant
This distinction doesn't actually matter in practice
questions.explain: This deliberately shifts the default toward removing access rather than assuming it's still needed.

questions.q: How does access review connect to Lesson 61 (PII masking) and Lesson 62 (secrets management)?
options: Masking controls who sees sensitive values and secrets management protects specific credentials; access reviews protect the broader accounts that could bypass or request those controls in the first place
Access reviews are unrelated to either of those two lessons
Access reviews replace the need for masking and secrets management entirely
Only secrets management connects to access reviews, not PII masking
questions.explain: None of Chapter 3's individual security lessons fully works without this recurring check behind it.
